title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 11 (Omitted — Historical Commencement of Business)

content.overview: Section 11 of the Companies Act, 2013 (as originally enacted) dealt with commencement of business and was later omitted. The functional regime for commencement of business is now primarily in Section 10A. Exam answers must use current law and not treat the omitted s. 11 as operative.
content.glance: Note that s. 11 has been omitted; point to s. 10A as the current commencement-of-business provision; warn against relying on repealed text.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 11 (Omitted — Historical Commencement of Business). Section 11 of the Companies Act, 2013 (as originally enacted) dealt with commencement of business and was later omitted. The functional regime for commencement of business is now primarily in Section 10A. Exam answers must use current law and not treat the omitted s. 11 as operative. Do not apply the omitted text. State that the section is not in force and name the current provision if the Act supplies one. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Original Role of Section 11
sections.body: As originally enacted, s. 11 regulated commencement of business after incorporation.

sections.heading: Omission
sections.body: Section 11 was omitted by amendment; it is no longer operative.

sections.heading: Current Law — Section 10A
sections.body: Commencement of business is now governed by s. 10A (declaration and office verification).

examples.title: Reliance on omitted section
examples.body: An answer cites s. 11 as the current commencement rule. That is incorrect; s. 11 is omitted and s. 10A applies.

hypotheticals.question: Is Section 11 still good law for commencement of business?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 11 has been omitted. Apply Section 10A.

misconceptions.trap: Section 11 still governs commencement of business.
misconceptions.correction: Section 11 is omitted; the current provision is Section 10A.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 11 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Note that s. 11 is omitted. II. Identify s. 10A as the current rule. III. Apply s. 10A to the facts. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Status of s. 11 (omitted); current provision s. 10A; application; precise relief.

examTips: Always flag that s. 11 is omitted.
